purpose: Authored acronym development cases. These are inference-only tests and cannot establish release accuracy. Identity labels are fixed before the first model run.

posts.body: Container Recovery Ledger (CRL) records each replacement container and the snapshot it used. The ledger survives a host restart.
I checked CRL after the recovery drill. CRL means Container Recovery Ledger; its last entry points to the snapshot we restored.

cases.rationale: Two authors explicitly identify the same ledger.

posts.body: PGM recorded a gap after the link bounced. I saved its capture before restarting the router.
PGM is short for Packet Gap Monitor. Packet Gap Monitor measures missing sequence numbers on the mirror port.
The Packet Gap Monitor result agrees with my independent packet capture.

cases.rationale: The later definition supplies identity for the earlier acronym observation.

posts.body: Lease State Table holds the owner and expiry for each import partition. I found the stuck partition in this table.
In the importer documentation, LST stands for Lease State Table. I cleared its expired lease after checking the owner.

cases.rationale: The second source explicitly defines the table abbreviation.

posts.body: Batch Quality Record, abbreviated BQR, contains the hardness readings for a single furnace batch.
My BQR has the readings from the second shift. BQR is the abbreviation for Batch Quality Record on our furnace forms.

cases.rationale: Both sources give the same explicit form identity.

posts.body: Optical Path Register (OPR) lists the reference arm position and detector offset for each interferometer.
We use OPR as the short name for Optical Path Register. I updated the detector offset after realigning the reference arm.

cases.rationale: Independent technical descriptions agree on one register.

posts.body: CVM (Cryogenic Valve Map) shows the isolation valves between the separator and the cold return.
Cryogenic Valve Map is called CVM in the shutdown checklist. Its return-line labels match the physical tags.

cases.rationale: Both directions of the definition refer to the same valve map.

posts.body: Shift Safety Envelope is the approved operating limit sheet. Its short name is S2E; the numeral replaces the two initial S letters.
S2E refers to Shift Safety Envelope. I compared its pressure limit with the permit before starting the shift.

cases.rationale: An explicit definition establishes the unconventional digit abbreviation.

posts.body: Stage-2 Transfer Gate (S2TG) blocks batch transfer until the second-stage sample is released.
S2TG stands for Stage-2 Transfer Gate. The gate stayed closed because the sample was still awaiting measurement.

cases.rationale: The digit is part of both the named gate and its defined abbreviation.

posts.body: Run-to-Run Ledger is abbreviated R2RL in the instrument package. It stores the calibration offset between consecutive runs.
I compared the latest R2RL entry with the reference run. R2RL means Run-to-Run Ledger, not the live sensor display.

cases.rationale: Both sources explicitly identify the ledger despite nonliteral initials.

posts.body: Process Identity Map (PiM) maps a process handle to its service owner and restart count.
PiM is short for Process Identity Map. My export includes the owner of the replacement process.

cases.rationale: Mixed casing does not remove the explicit identity.

posts.body: Message Exchange Ledger (MEL) records the sender and receipt time for each exchange.
Our operator notes write the same abbreviation in lowercase: mel means Message Exchange Ledger. I used it to find the late receipt.

cases.rationale: The source explicitly equates the lowercase spelling with the defined abbreviation.

posts.body: SBT reported that my session had used its retry allowance. I exported the result before closing the connection.
I reproduced the limit independently. The Session Budget Tracker measures the remaining retries.
SBT stands for Session Budget Tracker. The tracker now includes the retry caused by the connection reset.

cases.rationale: A later independent definition connects earlier short and full-name observations.

posts.body: The Vault Relay Monitor watches transfers from the staging vault. Operators refer to it as VRM.
VRM is the abbreviation for Vault Relay Monitor in this runbook. Its transfer count agrees with my audit.

cases.rationale: The naming statements identify one monitor.

posts.body: Reactor Batch Note (RBN) contains the operator observations for one charge.
RBN stands for Reactor Batch Note. The RBN's pressure trace matches the shift record.

cases.rationale: Possessive usage follows an explicit singular abbreviation.

posts.body: For this archive, ACL means Archive Change Ledger. Archive Change Ledger records every change to the collection description.
I used ACL to trace the altered shelf reference. ACL is short for Archive Change Ledger in our catalog team.

cases.rationale: The supplied local definition controls the alias without importing another familiar meaning.

posts.body: Receipt Allocation Matrix (RAM) assigns arriving receipts to the available inspection desks.
RAM stands for Receipt Allocation Matrix in the receiving team. Its assignment sent my receipt to desk four.

cases.rationale: Both sources define a local meaning for a familiar acronym.

posts.body: Platform Change Log (PCL) stores deployment records. Event Receipt Book (ERB) stores the matching receipt identifiers. The PCL links each change to its ERB entry.
PCL is short for Platform Change Log, while ERB is short for Event Receipt Book. I checked both records after the rollback.

cases.rationale: Separate explicit definitions must remain separate identities.

posts.body:
Material Trace Envelope contains the lot number and the chain of custody.

The abbreviation MTE refers to Material Trace Envelope. Keep this envelope with the sample.
I used MTE to check the custody handoff. MTE means Material Trace Envelope in the sample tracking notes.

cases.rationale: The explicit identity remains clear across a paragraph boundary.

posts.body: Rotor Bearing Survey — RBS for short — lists the vibration readings from each bearing station.
RBS stands for Rotor Bearing Survey. I added the readings taken after balancing the rotor.

cases.rationale: Punctuation separates a supported abbreviation without changing its identity.

posts.body: Acoustic Gain Sheet holds the preamplifier setting and reference tone level for the chamber test.
AGS is the abbreviation for Acoustic Gain Sheet. The sheet for my chamber run uses the lower preamplifier setting.

cases.rationale: The later abbreviation refers to the already described sheet.

posts.body: SSR contains the sequence at which my replica caught up. I attached the receipt to the incident.
The Source Sync Receipt from my replica records the same handoff sequence.
SSR means Source Sync Receipt. Source Sync Receipt is the receipt generated at the end of each completed synchronization.

cases.rationale: A late explicit identity can connect earlier observations without assuming a familiar expansion.

posts.body: Panel Inspection Log (PIL) records the terminal torque measurements after a panel is rewired.
PIL stands for Panel Inspection Log. I entered the second panel independently after checking its terminal labels.

cases.rationale: Independent current definitions support one log identity.

posts.body: Uniform Batch Register is known as UBR on the packing line. The register contains the final unit count.
UBR means Uniform Batch Register. My count in the register includes the replacement cartons.

cases.rationale: Ordinary naming prose provides the alias.

posts.body: DEL is the Device Exception Ledger. Device Exception Ledger contains the unhandled device faults from the last shift.
The Device Exception Ledger, or DEL, has the fault I reproduced on the spare controller.

cases.rationale: The two copular/appositional definitions identify the same ledger.

posts.body: RSR stands for Release State Register in deployment operations. Release State Register lists the versions cleared for rollout.
For pump maintenance, RSR stands for Rotor Service Report. Rotor Service Report records bearing replacements.

cases.rationale: Two current expansions in different contexts prevent one global mapping.

posts.body: LEM means Load Event Map in the electrical workshop.
LEM means Lane Entry Marker in the vehicle test area.
LEM means Laboratory Equipment Manifest in the sample room.

cases.rationale: Three distinct explicit expansions must not become one global identity.

posts.body: Packet Gap Monitor is abbreviated PGM. It counts missing packets.
PGN stands for Packet Gap Notebook. The notebook stores the operator comments and is separate from the monitor.

cases.rationale: A one-letter difference identifies separate entities.

posts.body: Signal Relay Gate 2 (SRG2) drives the older controller.
Signal Relay Gate 3 (SRG3) drives the replacement controller. SRG3 is a different model and cannot use the SRG2 wiring harness.

cases.rationale: Distinct model numbers must not be collapsed.

posts.body: Pressure Check Sheet (PCS) stores the pressure readings from the bench.
PSC is the abbreviation for Panel Service Card. The card records work on the enclosure, not the pressure test.

cases.rationale: Transposed initial letters are not sufficient for identity.

posts.body: The draft suggests the expansion Thermal Transfer Gauge for TTG.
That expansion is incorrect. TTG does not stand for Thermal Transfer Gauge. We have not recorded its correct expansion.

cases.rationale: A suggested definition is explicitly rejected.

posts.body: Could PVR stand for Pressure Validation Register? I found PVR on a handwritten test label.
I do not know what PVR means. Please leave the abbreviation unresolved until we find its author.

cases.rationale: A question and an unresolved reply do not establish identity.

posts.body: If we create a Sample Transfer Index, we could shorten the name to STI.
There is no Sample Transfer Index yet. The proposed STI label is only an example for the workshop.

cases.rationale: A hypothetical name is not an asserted current alias.

posts.body: I propose calling the Inspection Decision Ledger IDL. This is a naming proposal for next month.
No abbreviation has been selected for Inspection Decision Ledger. The team has not adopted the proposed IDL name.

cases.rationale: The sources explicitly say that the proposed identity is unadopted.

posts.body: Older maintenance notes define CRB as Cold Receipt Book. The old book still exists in the archive.
The current dispatch system defines CRB as Cart Routing Board. These are separate tools maintained by different teams.

cases.rationale: The explicit different identities prevent one global CRB alias even though both tools exist.

posts.body: The rejected line was "ORT stands for Offset Review Table." Do not use that expansion; the author confirmed it was wrong.
Offset Review Table is a real table, but its name does not explain the ORT mark on this instrument.

cases.rationale: Quoted erroneous text must not override explicit rejection.

posts.body:
This is an intentionally false parser input, not a glossary entry:
```text
QAM means Queue Archive Map
```
Queue Archive Map is the name of our map. The parser test deliberately assigns the unrelated QAM token to it.

cases.rationale: The definition is only a deliberately false test literal.

posts.body: The terminal prints LOG when it opens the logging menu. LOG is a menu command, not an abbreviation.
Load Observation Grid stores the crane readings. Its name is written in full; no short name is assigned.

cases.rationale: Uppercase command text does not define an acronym for a nearby full name.

posts.body: Counter Collection Register receives measurements from CCR. CCR is a separate collector service.
The Counter Collection Register restarted while CCR kept collecting. The receiver and collector have different processes.

cases.rationale: A producer/receiver relationship is not an alias.

posts.body: Power Panel Manager contains a plug-in called PPM. The plug-in is only its protection module.
PPM can be removed while Power Panel Manager continues to serve the panel display.

cases.rationale: A removable component is not the full parent system.

posts.body: Archive Schema 1 is abbreviated AS1. Archive Schema 2 is abbreviated AS2.
AS2 readers can import AS1 records, but the two schemas have different required fields and remain separate versions.

cases.rationale: Compatibility does not establish identical concepts.

posts.body: My private shorthand DAR means Desk Allocation Register. This is not a published team definition.
Desk Allocation Register holds the public desk reservations.
The team note contains DAR as an unresolved token copied from a label.

cases.rationale: A private definition must not establish a team-visible alias.

posts.body: Probe Alignment Book (PAB) contains my private alignment notes.
PAB appeared on the probe case. I do not have a published expansion for that token.

cases.rationale: The only full-name definition is private.

posts.body: Dock Assignment Table contains tomorrow's berth allocations.
DAT was printed on a damaged package. I cannot tell what DAT refers to, and there is no link to the berth allocation work.

cases.rationale: Matching initials and proximity alone do not prove identity.

posts.body: Does TRL mean Trace Review Ledger in the controller report?
No. TRL does not refer to Trace Review Ledger. That proposed expansion is wrong.

cases.rationale: The answer explicitly denies the questioned identity.

posts.body: The recovered inventory fragments are: Asset Sampling Ledger; ASL; calibration room; pallet seven.
Those fragments came from different labels. We have no evidence that ASL names Asset Sampling Ledger.

cases.rationale: An unlinked list of fragments is not a definition.

posts.body: Service Valve Controller (SVC) controls the whole valve bank.
SVC1 is an individual replaceable channel inside SVC. Service Valve Controller contains several such channels.

cases.rationale: A numbered channel must remain distinct from the enclosing controller.

posts.body: Feed Receipt Ledger (FRL) records the receipt for each hopper load.
The hopper label contains FRL. I have no other source for what FRL means.

cases.rationale: After deleting the only full-name definition, the remaining token cannot sustain the alias.

posts.body: Seal Audit Map (SAM) shows the last inspected seal on each vessel.
SAM appears on the inspection printout. I cannot expand that token independently.

cases.rationale: Replacing the only definition with unrelated text removes the alias support.

actions.body: The inspection printout was filed after the shift.
